policy.fact: Urea is sold at a fixed farm price; the government pays producers the difference to a normative cost under the New Urea Policy-2015 / New Investment Policy-2012: gas at the pooled price, energy at a plant-specific norm (Gcal per tonne) and a fixed-cost element. GNFC's energy norm was raised from 6.20 to 6.37 Gcal/t for 1-Apr-2025 to 31-Mar-2028 by a DoF notification of 30-Jun-2026 (~Rs61 cr for Apr-25 to Jun-26, booked in Q2FY27). The fixed-cost revision is still pending at industry level.

policy.fact: Nutrient Based Subsidy (P&K) for Kharif 2026 (1-Apr to 30-Sep-2026): N Rs47.32/kg, P Rs52.76/kg, S Rs3.16/kg, K Rs2.38/kg (Rabi 2025-26: N 43.02, P 47.96); outlay Rs41,534 cr (+12%); DAP farm price held at Rs1,350 per bag. For GNFC's ANP (20:20:0) the subsidy rises from Rs18,196/t to ~Rs20,016/t (+10%).

FY27 budget for fertiliser subsidy ~Rs1.71 lakh cr (urea ~Rs1.16 lakh cr, NBS ~Rs0.54 lakh cr). International prices Mar-25 to Mar-26: urea US$425 to 510/t, ammonia 454 to 562, DAP 640 to 708 (DoF bulletin).
Rabi 2026-27 NBS rates had not been announced by 30-Sep-2026.

chemicals.fact: The US-Iran war began in late February / early March 2026 (GNFC May-2026 call) and disrupted the Strait of Hormuz. Brent settled at US$102.59 on 29-Sep-2026, up ~14% in September, as the conflict and Hormuz risk continued; Gulf exports were back near pre-war levels via Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline.

China TDI: a major Shanghai producer raised its guidance price to RMB17,200/t on 8-Sep-2026 with volume restrictions; Wanhua raised MDI and TDI prices by US$300/t for South-East and South Asia from 14-Sep-2026.

GNFC marketing head (Aug-2026): 'Overall globally TDI production is quite high against the demand', so one-month shutdowns at Covestro and Wanhua will not move pricing; 'there is a shortage in the Indian market of TDI'.

Anti-dumping duty on TDI 80:20 from the EU and Saudi Arabia extended for five years by Notification 03/2026-Customs (ADD), 10-Feb-2026 (Covestro US$221/t, BorsodChem US$102/t, others US$265/t; Sadara US$218/t, others US$344/t); GNFC is the sole Indian producer and applicant. Duty on TDI from China, Japan and Korea (US$150-440/t) runs five years from 21-Sep-2022, i.e. to Sep-2027.
India's imports (kt): TDI 33 (FY19) to 68 (FY26, to Feb); aniline 88 to 279; acetic acid 937 to 1,250; methanol 1,987 to 3,304; ammonium nitrate 273 to 385 (peak 450 in FY24).
Ammonium nitrate demand grows 6-7% a year; ~4-4.5 lakh t imported; Chambal, Deepak Fertilisers and GNFC are adding capacity; government push on coal mining (explosives) supports demand.
China removed export-tax rebates on ~200-250 products incl. acetic acid and methanol, which should support Indian acetic acid prices.

Sanjeev Kumar, IAS takes charge as MD

moat: Only TDI producer in South Asia with ~60% of Indian demand; anti-dumping duties of US$100-440/t on imports; import-parity pricing.
Chinese TDI, aniline and acetic acid plants are far larger and use coal; GNFC's TDI-II has not covered its fixed costs at FY25-26 prices; aniline is uneconomic on its own.
Ammonia, nitric acids, CNA and syngas feed TDI, aniline, AN and formic acid on one site; oil, gas and coal flexibility.
Regulated returns; loss-making for six straight years because fixed costs and energy norms lag reality.
~Rs5,200 cr of treasury, no debt; but the state promoter decides where it goes.
critiques: Q4FY26-Q1FY27 profits are war-time profits; management itself says the situation 'can go either side'
Global TDI capacity exceeds demand; Chinese scale caps prices whenever the war premium fades
Fertiliser segment has lost money every year since FY21 and needs a fixed-cost revision the government has not given
Rs2,410 cr of surplus cash lent to a state finance company at ~7.25%; four MDs in 20 months
Rs7,000-8,000 cr phenol/BPA and other projects under study could absorb the cash at uncertain returns
gaps: No broker note dated Jul-Sep 2026 with target, method and estimates was found; JM Financial (Neutral, Rs580) and ICICI Securities (Neutral, Rs550) are cited only by a third-party blog without dates.
Named non-promoter holders above 1% in the Jun-2026 pattern not verified (BSE page blocked to automated access); Mar-2026 category split used.
Segment depreciation is not disclosed, so segment EBITDA cannot be built; we model segment EBIT.
Product-wise revenue and TDI realisations for FY27 to date are not disclosed beyond the quarterly price panel.
Kearney savings (Rs250-300 cr target) not quantified by management; we include only CCPP savings.
Incremental revenue/EBIT of the Rs2,800 cr projects is a management 'ballpark' at war-time prices (Rs1,200-1,500 cr revenue, Rs500-600 cr contribution).
Rabi 2026-27 NBS rates and the urea fixed-cost revision were not known by 30-Sep-2026.
China/Japan/Korea TDI anti-dumping duty expires Sep-2027; any sunset-review initiation was not public by 30-Sep-2026.
